blocks.text: In 1900 the German geneticist Karl Correns rediscovered Mendel's work and suggested the role of chromosomes in heredity. In 1902 the American scientist Walter Sutton proposed the chromosomal theory of inheritance.

blocks.title: Chromosomal theory of inheritance
blocks.text: Genes are found at specific locations on chromosomes. The behaviour of chromosomes during meiosis explains Mendel's laws of inheritance.

blocks.caption: Mendel's laws and chromosome behaviour
rows: Two factors for each character, one per gamete (segregation)
Homologous chromosomes, carrying the two alleles, separate into different gametes in meiosis I.
Different homologous pairs line up at random, so genes on different chromosomes assort independently.

blocks.prompt: Who proposed the chromosomal theory of inheritance, and when?
blocks.explanation: Walter Sutton, in 1902, after Karl Correns had rediscovered Mendel's work in 1900.

items: Correns 1900: Mendel rediscovered; Sutton 1902: chromosomal theory.
Genes sit at loci on chromosomes; meiosis explains Mendel's laws.
